items.readme:
Leonida Continued

Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord | Telegram

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. > [!NOTE] > **This is a continuation of [NotRexed's Leonida project](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida).** The original > author has left the project, and development continues here with its full commit history. Credit for the work up to > that point belongs to NotRexed and the contributors listed in the history. Discord: https://discord.gg/ETf4qj5acN Telegram: https://t.me/mandyport Original author's Git Mirror: https://git.notrexed.dev/notrexed/Leonida
## Project status **Early. The game does not boot yet.** Everything that can be done without the game's executable is in place, so work on booting can start as soon as one is available to a developer. | What | Status | |---|---| | Booting, story mode, anything playable | ❌ No | | Finding and checking your copy (Xbox Series 1.0.2.1) | ✅ Works | | Shaders: carve, unpack native RDNA2 code, disassemble | ✅ All 26,503 | | Shaders: RDNA2 → SPIR-V translation | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 translated**: 2,236 VS, 12,101 PS, 2,689 CS, 9,282 mesh, 195 geometry, with a per-shader metadata index for pipeline creation. The LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and the LLVM 23.1.3 Windows rerun at `43d0015` both translated all 26,503 ([Linux](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [Windows](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7074299915)). Translation and SPIR-V validation are separate steps; validation results are listed below. ⚠️ 23,841 are wave64: exact on 64-wide subgroups (AMD). On 32-wide subgroups (NVIDIA, Intel), compute and mesh shaders are exact with wave64 emulation (`--wave64-emulate`, on by default there); cross-half wave ops in vertex, pixel and geometry shaders are still approximate | | SPIR-V validation (`spirv-val`) | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 passed** in the LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and in the full-corpus rerun at `43d4703`, after `dcd8ecf` fixed the SPIR-V ID-bound error ([Linux rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [full-corpus rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/881#issuecomment-7075507328)). On Windows at `43d0015`, all 26,503 translated but 26,501 passed validation; the two ID-bound failures were fixed by `dcd8ecf`. The intermediate `dedd75c` run also passed 26,501. | | Shader translator checked on a real GPU | ⚠️ The hand-written GPU tests (vertex fetch, texture sampling, exports, ALU ops, partial-register ops, barycentrics, wave-uniform branches, compute LDS/barriers/buffer stores, wave64 masks) have been run on more than 30 GPU and driver combinations, with results in [#166](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/166): NVIDIA Turing, Ampere, Ada and Blackwell (Windows and Linux); AMD GCN3, RDNA1, RDNA2, RDNA3 and RDNA4 (Windows driver and RADV); Intel Gen9 (ANV); Apple M1 (MoltenVK, no geometry or mesh stages); and Mesa llvmpipe. Wave64 tests need 64-wide subgroups (AMD) or `LEONIDA_W64_EMULATE=1`. These are small test shaders: the game's own shaders are checked by `spirv-val` and by driver pipeline creation (`vk_pipeline_check`), not by their output | | Models (OBJ with real names, UVs, material references) | ✅ Exported. A ten-archive scan at decoder pin `e293917` recovered **382,781 models** with zero readback decode failures. This includes **343,327** models from `levels.rpf`. A full OBJ export of that archive is pending. See [recount and export scope](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). | | Texture dictionaries and world texture pools (DDS) | ✅ Exported. `rpf9dump` decodes BCPack BC1, BC3, BC4 and BC5 chunks in strict mode and skips BC6H, BC7 and chunks that need unconfirmed history; the assets stage then completes what it can with a clean-room decoder (`tools/bcpack.py`, which `tools/ttpf_assets.py` runs through `tools/ttpf_mips.py`) that rebuilds BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7, and records the rest as a `BCPackLimitation` in `manifest.json` (most BC6H/BC7 chunks and the unconfirmed-history ones need a local history table, which the repo does not ship) ([notes](docs/textures.md)) | | Audio banks (AWC: Opus, XMA2) | ✅ Exported whole. Opus repackaged **losslessly** as Ogg Opus; PCM (codec 0/2) as WAV; XMA2 decoded with ffmpeg. `--wav` adds 16-bit PCM WAV ([notes](docs/audio.md)) | | Music/radio config | ? Measured. **1,589** audio-config records with exact durations and AWC stream ids; station grouping and content-id lists; no per-track start offsets ([notes](docs/audio_config.md)) | | PE loader and import shims | ⚠️ Runs a stand-in executable end to end (`gta6rt --run`: CRT startup, statics, heap, files, threads, GDK imports through the shims, exit code back). Controllers through a GameInput shim on SDL3 (any controller SDL supports, rumble, DualSense trigger effects and lightbar; built when SDL3 is installed or with `-DLEONIDA_SDL3_FETCH=ON`, [notes](docs/gameinput.md)). `--trace-d3d12` logs every D3D12 call and its outcome for the first boot. Untested against the real executable | | Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan | ⚠️ In progress. A Vulkan-backed device behind the Xbox-ABI proxy creates queues, command lists, fences, descriptor heaps, committed, placed and reserved resources, render-target and depth views (3D targets included), texture views and samplers (2D, cube, 1D and 3D views, the depth and stencil planes of depth-stencil textures, packed formats such as B5G6R5, B4G4R4A4 and R9G9B9E5, buffer SRVs — raw, structured and typed; they go into the bindless set), root signatures, pipelines and query heaps, and draws run on Vulkan. Barriers, clears, uploads, copies (BC included), colour resolves, predication, CPU-side texture reads and writes, and occlusion, timestamp and pipeline-statistics queries run on Vulkan, checked on one GPU. The console-shaped command-list proxy, the measured `PresentX` queue slots (30/32, layout-detected) wired to the presentation core, and `AllocateUploadMemory` (list slot 148, a mapped-upload arena whose addresses translate to buffer device addresses in root descriptors and IA/SO views) cover the console-ABI surface the package measures. Still open: the console list tail and the descriptor-table record model ([plan](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)) | | Ray tracing (BVH) | ⚠️ In progress. `BuildRaytracingAccelerationStructure` builds BLASes and TLASes on the GPU in the console's XDXR BVH4 layout (the default; `LEONIDA_RT_AS=khr` uses Vulkan's own acceleration structures instead), which the translated shaders walk themselves through `image_bvh_intersect_ray` (all four triangle node types, TRI0-TRI3, with the barycentric remap byte); the GPU builder writes TRI0 and TRI1 leaves. Updates refit instead of rebuilding, and clone, compaction and the compacted/current postbuild sizes work; checked against a CPU reference on synthetic scenes. The build descriptions are recovered from the package's `XboxBvhBuilder.dll` ([notes](docs/xdxr.md)). The game's `*_bvh4.rpf` packs are measured: offline-built, dehydrated BLASes that rehydrate through that DLL with their geometry from the drawables in `levels.rpf` (measured on 8 of the 10 sampled BLAS; [notes](docs/bvh.md)). Not done in the builder: serialization. TRI1 pairing (no memory saved yet) and BOX16 nodes for `MINIMIZE_MEMORY` BLASes (an assumed switch) are in ([notes](docs/bvh.md)). Open: whether the game rehydrates the packs or rebuilds them ([#313](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/313)) | The table above is written by hand. To measure it on your own checkout (unit and runtime tests, which rows of the translator contract were confirmed on a GPU, measured imports, your corpus counts and, with `--github`, CI and the `D3D-` items), run `python -I tools/progress_dashboard.py --out ` and open `progress.html` ([notes](docs/progress_dashboard.md)). ## Platforms Nothing is playable on any platform yet (see *Project status*). What runs where today: | Platform | Today | |---|---| | Windows | Everything: `make_game.py`, the tools, and the runtime (`gta6rt` and the D3D12 → Vulkan layer) with its tests. | | Linux | The translator, the asset tools and the Vulkan GPU test tools build and run natively (tested on RADV and NVIDIA). The runtime is Windows code: it cross-compiles with clang-cl and xwin, and its tests run under Wine or Proton (*The Windows runtime on Linux, under Wine or Proton* below). The game is meant to run the same way, under Wine or Proton with the D3D12 layer on native Vulkan (#217). `./Build.sh` starts the build; [docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md) has the packages and the steps. | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | The Python tools and the Vulkan test tools run natively, on MoltenVK (Homebrew) or KosmicKrisp. The runtime is Windows code and runs as on Linux, under Wine: CrossOver, arm64 with FEX or x86-64 under Rosetta (#1706, #1707, #1924; #3119 fixes the last loader tests there). Known gaps: no geometry stage and no `VK_EXT_mesh_shader` (those tests are skipped), 32-wide subgroups (wave64 shaders run emulated), and MoltenVK's float handling (`PerVertexKHR`, NaN compares, -0, the cost of `NoContraction`); [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) lists each (#2947). | | AMD RDNA1 (RX 5000) | A supported target: close to the console's RDNA2, and its 64-wide subgroups run the wave64 shaders natively. RX 5700 XT results pass the GPU test suite (#146); on RADV, pixel shaders without fragment barycentrics have a known difference (*Known problems* in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)) (#330). | GPU results from every platform are collected in #166; how to run the tests is in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). ## How to build The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy. **The easy way:** 1. Install the prerequisites below. 2. Download this project **with its submodule**: `git clone --recursive https://github.com/ubiquitarianism/leonida`. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out `third_party/rpf9-explorer`. The build fetches it if `git` is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do. 3. Double-click **`Build.bat`**. On Linux or macOS, run **`./Build.sh`** from a terminal instead (see [docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md) for Linux). It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to `Documents\Leonida`. A stopped build continues where it left off. Your game folder is the one that holds `MicrosoftGame.Config` and the `.rpf` archives, as plain files. **Prerequisites:** - **Your own copy** of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1. - **Windows 10/11 x64**, with about **400 GB** free for work files (an assets export alone measured about 337 GB before its audio step, in about 2 h 35 min). Disk sizes here are as Windows Explorer shows them, which are GiB: 400 GiB is about 430 GB in decimal units. They can go on another drive with `--work`. - [Python 3.12+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (tick "Add python.exe to PATH"). - [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0). - [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/), for `spirv-as` / `spirv-val`. - [LLVM 21+](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases) with the **AMDGPU target** for `llvm-mc`. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, `scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1` builds a native `llvm-mc.exe` with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets `LLVM_MC`; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use [conda](https://docs.conda.io/): `conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools` (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) used version 23.1.6), then set `LLVM_MC` to the full path of the `llvm-mc.exe` it installs (`where.exe llvm-mc` shows it once the environment is active; in PowerShell a bare `where` is `Where-Object`). Or install `llvm-21` in WSL and set `LLVM_MC` to the whole command, `LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc"` (see [docs/design.md](docs/design.md#disassembling-shaders)). On Linux, `llvm-mc` on PATH is enough, and so is a versioned distribution install such as Ubuntu's `llvm-21` (`llvm-mc-21`, `/usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc`). - Visual Studio 2022 with **Desktop development with C++** and the **Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer**, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare). - [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for `--wav`). **Is this PC strong enough?** [Can I Run Leonida](https://assttro.github.io/can-i-run-leonida/) is a lightweight browser-based checker that compares your PC against reference profiles. It's a rough estimate, not a benchmark. **Low disk space:** the ~400 GB figure is for the full build. To *run* the port, `--stages check,shaders,runtime` needs about 30 GB; the `assets` stage (~370 GB) is only for the asset tools, and `--wav` adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). `--work` and `--out` can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs `gta6rt --overlay `; `--overlay` is a `gta6rt` option, not a `make_game.py` one. Leave the `.s` files in `work/shaders/dxbc/disasm` in place: the next run checks them against the list in `disasm.done` and disassembles the missing ones again (all of them for a folder whose `disasm.done` predates that list), then translates every shader again. A `disasm` folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it. **Disk space and drives:** the build uses three folders, and each can be on its own drive: | Folder | Flag | What is in it | Size | Read when playing | |---|---|---|---|---| | your package | `--game` | your copy of the game; only read, never written | as copied | yes, in place (`game_path.txt`) | | work | `--work` (default `\work`) | `shaders` (carved, disassembled, translated) and `assets` (exports) | about 30 GB + about 370 GB | only `shaders\spirv` (`shader_path.txt`) | | port | `--out` (default `Documents\Leonida`) | `gta6rt.exe`, its DLL, the path files, the pipeline cache, `overlay` | small | yes | The free-space check before a build counts the `--work` drive only, because that is where the large files go. Nothing in `\assets` is read by the game, so with a small SSD you can keep what the game loads on the SSD and put the exports on a hard drive, in two runs: ```powershell # on the SSD: the package, the port and the translated shaders (about 30 GB of work files) python -I make_game.py --game "S:\Games\package" --out "S:\Games\Leonida" --work "S:\Games\Leonida\work" --stages check,shaders,runtime,pipelines # on the hard drive: the asset exports (about 370 GB), only for the asset tools python -I make_game.py --game "S:\Games\package" --out "S:\Games\Leonida" --work "H:\leonida-assets" --stages check,assets ``` The second run does not rebuild the runtime, so `shader_path.txt` keeps pointing at the SSD. Pass the same `--work` again for later runs of each stage so they resume. A single `--work "H:\leonida-work"` also works; the game then loads its translated shaders from that drive. **From a terminal**, with the same behaviour and more control: ```powershell python -I make_game.py --find # list the copies found on this PC python -I make_game.py --pick # choose the game folder in a folder dialog python -I make_game.py --check # check your copy, build nothing python -I make_game.py --check --full-check # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow) python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work" python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets # only some stages python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large) python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off # auto (default), on or off; see below ``` `--wave64-emulate` decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, `auto`, asks `vulkaninfo` (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With `--mesh-compute`, only compute subgroup support is needed. On AMD's Windows driver, `auto` uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or `vulkaninfo` is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support. The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. `auto` can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use `--wave64-emulate on` to force emulation or `--wave64-emulate off` to force native wave64. Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: `--no-float-controls` (drop `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve`, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without `shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32`; needs PR #664's translator flag), `--bary-fallback` (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`), `--texel-offset-fallback` (fold `image_sample*_o` offsets into the coordinate, for devices without `VK_KHR_maintenance8`) and `--mesh-compute` (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`; on by itself on Intel's Windows Vulkan driver, whose native mesh draws crash, BUILD-2202, unless `--native-mesh`). Each is documented in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs. The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information. The build also records which decoder (the `third_party/rpf9-explorer` commit and the `tools/rpf9dump` sources) exported each archive's models and textures and each texture pool. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models, textures and pools are exported once more after upgrading. Stages: `check` always runs first; then `shaders`, `assets` and `runtime` run together when selected (they do not depend on each other). `pipelines` starts once the translated shaders are ready and, when this run includes runtime, that stage has finished rebuilding `vk_pipeline_check`, so it can overlap the rest of assets; it creates every translated shader on your GPU driver, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to `pipeline_cache.bin` in `--out` (the runtime doesn't load that cache yet, so it doesn't speed up the first boot). The shader translation is the longest CPU step: it runs on `--jobs` processes (half the CPU threads by default). When shaders and assets share the machine, that budget is split between them and passed to `rpf9dump` as `--jobs`; a solo assets run still lets `rpf9dump` use every core. Progress lines include percent and a rough ETA for translation shards, asset steps, and overall stage completion. On an interactive terminal, a LEONIDA setup screen lets you set jobs and whether stages overlap, then a key-switchable per-stage log view (`1`–`4` / `Tab`) keeps parallel output demuxed; full stage logs go under `work/logs/`. Use `--no-tui` (or redirect stdout) for the plain console. `--wav` is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to `work\assets\audio\wav` after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes. ### Vulkan diagnostics on Linux With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed: ```sh cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel ./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv ``` Pass the directory containing `index.json` and the translated SPIR-V files to `vk_pipeline_check`. `make_game.py` runs on Linux too. The `pipelines` stage uses the `vk_pipeline_check` built above (`runtime/build/linux`, or `runtime/build`), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing. ### Running the loader on Linux The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every push to `main` that changes `runtime/`, and on demand from the Actions tab (the `wine` job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the `runtime` stage cross-builds it into `runtime/build/windows` with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#known-problems); plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as `clang-cl-21`) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin) lays out, in `XWIN_DIR` or `~/.local/share/xwin-sdk` ([docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#the-windows-runtime-on-linux-under-wine-or-proton) has the one-time `xwin` command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the `runtime-windows` artifact of that workflow's `windows` job, unzipped: ```sh python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows ``` Either way it copies `gta6rt.exe` and `gta6rt_tls_host.dll` into `--out` and writes `gta6rt.sh` next to them, which starts `gta6rt.exe` with `wine`, or with the Wine named by `WINE` (for Proton, its `files/bin/wine`). The same option skips the build on Windows. On Linux, run `/gta6rt.sh --dry-run` to inspect the packaged title's imports, then `/gta6rt.sh --init` to check TLS callbacks and DLL initialization. Use `/gta6rt.sh --run` for startup. These commands use the package in `game_path.txt`, the port's `overlay` for writes, and Vulkan by default. When the Vulkan backend is selected with `LEONIDA_D3D12=vulkan`, the packaged runtime finds the translated shaders in `/shaders/spirv` using `shader_path.txt` beside `gta6rt.exe`. Set `LEONIDA_SHADERS` to use another directory. ## How it works | Piece | What it does | Where | |---|---|---| | Version check | Every package file's name, size and SHA-256 for each supported version | `game/`, `make_game.py` | | Shader pipeline | Carves DXBC containers from `shaders.rpf` without its encrypted table of contents. Unpacks the `XBCH` → `FSSM` native RDNA2 program, disassembles it with LLVM (`gfx1013`) and translates it to SPIR-V | `tools/shader_carve.py` ([optional Rust scanner](tools/shader_carve_native/README.md)), `fssm_unpack.py`, `shader_disasm.py`, `rdna2spirv.py` | | Asset export | Finds validated resources inside RPF9 archives and the loose `.ttpf` texture pools | `tools/rpf9dump` (on rpf9-explorer's Core) | | Runtime | Maps the PE image, resolves imports to shims (GDK, XMem, `d3d12_xs`) | `runtime/` | | Research tools | PE/RTTI inspection, raw carving, texture tiling probes, GPU test harnesses | `tools/`, `runtime/test/` | | Progress dashboard | One offline page of what passes, what changed since it last passed and what blocks next, built from test results and the docs' own tables; nothing is written inside the repo | `tools/progress_dashboard.py` | Localized string tables are decoded by `tools/text_tables.py` ([docs/text.md](docs/text.md)); their language is guessed from script (kana, hangul, CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic) or Latin words, and subtitles are joined to dialogue lines across languages. The translator's runtime contract (user SGPRs, push constants, memory model, bindless images, vertex fetch, system values) and all the format notes are in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md); the format, asset, runtime and validation notes are indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). The Xbox D3D12 plan is in [docs/d3d12_vulkan.md](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md). Audio bank formats and the export tools are in [docs/audio.md](docs/audio.md); [docs/related_projects.md](docs/related_projects.md) records the prior art we may read and the licence limits on it. ## Want to help? The biggest open pieces: - **Shader translator on hardware**: compute, mesh and geometry now translate (see the translator contract in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)); still open are the vertex-shader input layout (`v0` = `VertexIndex` is unverified if the console runs VS as NGG) and wave64 cross-half code in VS/PS/GS on 32-wide subgroups. - **Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan**: mesh-shader draws, indirect draw state and stream output are still open; #313 tracks the remaining method surface, and nothing has been checked against the real executable yet ([plan and status](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)). - **Model recovery**: investigate the 71 unrecovered fragment candidates in [`levels.rpf`](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Never attach game files, extracted assets or generated shaders to issues or pull requests. ## Credits - [Leonida](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida) by NotRexed and contributors: the original project, which this repository continues. - [rpf9-explorer](https://github.com/breadbbbb/rpf9-explorer) by breadbbbb: the RPF9 model, texture-pool and AWC decoders used by `tools/rpf9dump` (git submodule). - [Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa) (MIT): GFX10 resource-descriptor layout (`tools/gfx10_formats.json`), and the ACO/RADV rules used as reference for 16-bit results and shader system registers. - [libHttpClient](https://github.com/microsoft/libHttpClient) (MIT) by Microsoft: the XTaskQueue/XAsync implementation in `third_party/xtaskqueue`, used by the offline `xgameruntime` shim. - [LLVM](https://llvm.org/): AMDGPU disassembler. - Logo: ["Grand Theft Auto VI" icon by SlyDevil](https://www.steamgriddb.com/icon/122618) on SteamGridDB. - [SPIRV-Tools](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Tools): assembly and validation. Grand Theft Auto and all related names are trademarks of their owners. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by them. ## License GPLv3 (or any later version). See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party code keeps its own license.

items.readme: # Xbox Emulator **Running the Xbox Series X|S library on PC. A continuation of [drycheetah84/TomBox](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox).** The runtime reimplements the console's platform layer (Xbox-flavoured Direct3D 12, precompiled RDNA2 shaders, unified-memory textures, system libraries) so dumped, already-decrypted Xbox Series X|S builds run as normal Windows processes. It is not tied to any single title. This repo tracks our continuation — new titles brought up, platform calls extended, shader stages unlocked. Uses legally obtained, already-decrypted dumps. The runtime does no key extraction or package decryption. **Source code:** the emulator's Rust workspace is in this repo: [`crates/`](crates/), [`tools/`](tools/) and `Cargo.toml`. It contains no game files, binaries or build output. **Contributing:** pull requests are welcome, especially console library functions still marked missing in the [library map](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. ## Status [![system functions](docs/img/badge-imports.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![Direct3D 12.x methods](docs/img/badge-d3d12x.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![RDNA2 instructions](docs/img/badge-instructions.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![shaders translated](docs/img/badge-shaders.svg)](#tested-titles) [![shader stages](docs/img/badge-stages.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![milestones](docs/img/badge-milestones.svg)](#milestones) [![titles examined](docs/img/badge-titles.svg)](#tested-titles) [![Xbox console libraries](docs/img/badge-console.svg)](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md) [![progress map](docs/img/progress.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) One square per item. The first four sections use upstream's definitions so the numbers stay comparable: green = done, amber = partial (a stub, a forwarder, or not verified to work), grey = not done — imported system functions of the Fortnite EXE, Direct3D 12.x interface methods, RDNA2 shader instructions the decoder knows, and the eight shader stages (mesh and amplification still grey). The fifth section is ours and covers Xbox console libraries only: the exports of the console OS DLLs (EmbeddedXvd of every analysed title, union, so the newest console OS sets the surface) that no same-named DLL in a PC's C:\Windows\System32 exports, so console-only DLLs (d3d12_xs, xg_xs, xmem, AcpHal, chad, xapu, xcrdapi, the *legacy variants, ...) count in full and modified PC DLLs (kernel32, advapi32, mfplat, ...) only for their console-only exports, plus the GDK wrappers the emulator redirects; plain Windows DLLs (ntdll, msvcrt, ucrtbase, combase, ...) are not shown. Coloured implemented / forwarded / stub / missing; lighter squares are functions an analysed title imports. Per-title import coverage likewise counts only imports from console libraries. Generated by tools/progress/gen.py; per-function tables in docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md, headline numbers in tools/progress/summary.json. ## Milestones Counted live by `tools/progress/gen.py`; full table with evidence in [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md). | Milestone | State | |---|---| | All imported system functions covered (671/671) | done | | Full title shader sweep translated (105,506/105,506) | done | | All Direct3D 12.x methods covered | in progress (map) | | All RDNA2 instructions verified | in progress (map) | | All shader stages (Mesh, Amplification) | in progress (map) | | All Xbox console libraries covered | in progress (map) | | Fortnite boots, first frames, login, hotfix, mode select, BR lobby | done (7 run milestones) | | 3D scene correct | not reached | | Keyboard / controller input | not reached | | Audio | not reached | | Gameplay | not reached | | A second title running | not reached | ## Tested titles | Title | Build | Result | |---|---|---| | Fortnite (Chapter 2 Season 4) | 2.0.1461.7919 | Boots, logs in to a private server, reaches the lobby. 2D interface correct. 3D scene lit but the character material is wrong and bloom shows artifacts. No audio. Not playable. On this machine (2026-11-21): boots, first frames, window on the primary monitor, login complete, hotfix success, game-mode select, Battle Royale lobby (`UI.State.Athena.Frontend`). | | XDefiant | dump examined | **Not run.** Imports and console OS (10.0.22000) mapped in [docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md); new modules include XCurl, Bink2Scarlett, chad (XDsp*), xapu (XApu*). | | Grand Theft Auto VI | 1.0.2.1 | **Not run** (dump has no executable). Shader package examined: 26,503 shaders, plain compressed Xbox shader containers. Of a 4,000-shader sample all disassemble cleanly; ~⅓ of vertex shaders translate. Blockers: mesh shaders, shaders without root signatures. | ## Our local state - [docs/DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md) — chronological log - [docs/BLOCKERS.md](docs/BLOCKERS.md) — standing walls - [docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md) — per-library, per-function status (generated) - [docs/LIBRARY_DISCOVERY.md](docs/LIBRARY_DISCOVERY.md) — what the dumps contain ## Credit Upstream: [drycheetah84/TomBox](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox) (base commit `7e8064f`). # VIctory fork (work in progress)

A work-in-progress fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a
compatibility layer that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from
files the user supplies. This fork follows upstream
`main` and adds fixes aimed at one goal: getting the game's world to render
correctly and playably on one particular PC.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's
developer or publisher.

## Credits

- **[VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory)** by Marvisak and its
  contributors is the base of everything here: the loader, the runtime
  services, the Direct3D 12 back end and the shader recompiler. Licensed
  GPL-3.0-or-later; so is this fork. Upstream's history is kept intact below
  the single commit that carries this fork's changes.
- **[XCL](https://github.com/ivall/xcl)** by ivall and its contributors
  (GPL-2.0-only) was used as a reference for how the same title behaves under
  another layer. Fixes inspired by it were written anew in VIctory's code.
- This fork's changes were developed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

## Status of this fork (2026-11-25)

**Not playable yet: 2.5 to 4 frames per second, and shadowed areas are black.**
Tested on one machine: Windows 11, Intel i7-14700KF, NVIDIA RTX 4070 12 GB,
32 GB RAM. The Series X profile is used throughout.

| Stage | State in this fork |
|-------|--------------------|
| Boot, menus, start screen | works, 30 fps (as upstream) |
| Opening cutscene | plays from start to finish, in order, lit: title cards, credits cards, night and dusk shots |
| Saves | the game autosaves a checkpoint and loads it again |
| First gameplay scene (the prologue) | renders: characters, textures, sky, sunlit exterior; HUD, pause menu and pad input work |
| Light in shadow | missing: the game's ray-traced bounce light and ray-traced lamp and sun shadows do not run yet, so anything the sun does not hit directly is black |
| Frame rate in the world | 2-4 fps: 420-450 ms per frame by default, 240-350 ms with the newer switches (`VICTORY_RELAY=2`, or `VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=3 VICTORY_WIDE_BACK=1 VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MIN_MB=1 VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MB=1024`); it started at 3-6 seconds per frame |
| Stability | no driver hang or device loss in normal runs (a hang introduced by the wave64 update was found and fixed: its barrier form for 64-lane programs is now off unless `VICTORY_WAVE_WIDE=1`) |

### What this fork changed (summary)

Rendering:
- Meshlet culling read its scene buffers as the wrong kind of view, so the world drew almost nothing; fixed.
- Per-draw descriptor tables could run out, after which draws used slots never made for them and the card hung; fixed.
- Light packed by the game's compute shaders was read back through empty copies (sky, probes, fog); fixed for every mip level and layer.
- The fog reconstruction, shadow-mask, hair, blend-shape skinning, fire and several material programs did not translate; fixed.
- Gathers at a named mip level (with and without an offset) read level 0; fixed.
- Implicit-level samples outside pixel shaders produced invalid DXIL in 730 compute programs; fixed.
- Rectangle lists, depth and stencil twins for depth textures written by compute, texture read-backs.
- Ray tracing, in progress and off by default: the game's own structure-builder programs translate, title memory can be read by raw address from shaders, the hardware ray/box and ray/triangle test is emulated in DXIL (checked against a reference on the GPU), and 59 of the 64 trace programs translate. Nothing is lit by it yet. See [docs/fork-ray-tracing.md](docs/fork-ray-tracing.md).

Speed and memory:
- Waits for memory values, write-watch queries and page queries no longer walk page tables per call.
- Large title buffers get a copy in card memory, with shader writes found by hashing on the card.
- Submissions can be sent ahead of the wait for the card (`VICTORY_LATE_WAIT`), with a relay thread that lands results as the card finishes (`VICTORY_RELAY`): in a first five-minute run the card's idle time behind the submitting thread fell from about 136 to 30 ms per frame.
- Title memory can be opened as a graphics heap so that buffers are used in place instead of copied (`VICTORY_INPLACE`, first stage only; a probe confirmed the approach on the test GPU).
- The bindless texture queue no longer uploads stale views; the view table no longer grows without bound; the pipeline library is mapped instead of read into memory.
- An intermittent device loss was traced to the pipeline library file being replaced while mapped; fixed.

- Translated shaders get clean-up passes over the finished module (dead code, constant folding, reuse of values, branch facts); the pack's host instruction count falls by about 43 %, worth about 20 ms of GPU time per frame on the test machine (`VICTORY_SHADER_OPT=0` turns them off).

Most of the newer speed changes sit behind environment switches that are off
by default (`VICTORY_LATE_WAIT`, `VICTORY_RELAY`, `VICTORY_WIDE_BACK`,
`VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MIN_MB`, `VICTORY_INPLACE`, `VICTORY_BVH_BUILDER`, ...).
Each is described in a comment where it is read.

### Known problems

- Everything in shadow is black (see above).
- The interior of the first gameplay room is sometimes not drawn after the cutscene hands over to gameplay.
- Around 24 GB of memory is in use during play.
- A few style lints are switched off for this fork in the workspace `Cargo.toml` until the newer code is tidied.
- Many changes here are specific to this title and this GPU, and some are marked `shortcut:` in the code where they approximate what the console does.

Everything below this line is upstream VIctory's own README, unchanged; its
status section describes upstream, not this fork.

---

# VIctory

Runs the title (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files
the user supplies.

The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies
the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where
it can and on first use where it must (shaders). See
[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Status (2026-11-23)

**Not playable yet.** The title boots, runs its menus at its own 30 fps and
loads the world, where rendering fails.

| Stage | State |
|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |
| Loading into the world (about 50 s) | works |
| The world (first mission's intro) | reached and runs with indirect draws; its title card renders, the scene after it is still dark; 0.5-1.8 s per frame |

Tested on one machine: Windows 11, AMD RX 6700 XT.

> **Warning.** Entering the world on a real GPU can currently hang it, and
> Windows then resets the display driver (every monitor goes black for a
> moment). To look further, use a diagnostics build with
> `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1`, which renders on the software adapter.

What each part does today and what it still needs:

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Loader | Runs the title's executable and its DLLs in our process; crash reports name the faulting code and are kept in `crashes.log` | – |
| Runtime services | One signed-in offline user, licences, packages, saves that survive a kill at any step, text entry dialog | Speech is silent; the dialog and relaunch are untested live |
| Network | Offline by design: the title cannot reach the network | – |
| Files and streaming | Archives and streamed data read, zlib and BCPack decoded in parallel | Loading is limited by writes into title memory |
| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |
| Audio | Menu, video and loading sound; XMA voices and Opus streams decode | Reverb is silent; Opus results unverified against the title |
| GPU: menus | Draws, compute and presentation on host D3D12; only changed title memory is copied | Frame pacing drifts on one screen in release builds |
| GPU: world | Mesh pipelines, shader-written buffers, descriptor lifetimes, indirect execution (arguments clamped), pipelines made by worker threads and kept on disk | Most of the scene is still missing (untranslated shaders drop draws); frames take seconds; real queries, depth bounds, HDR and scaling are missing |
| Shaders | Console GPU code recompiled to DXIL at first use, cached on disk. Menus: all. World: mesh 8,191 of 8,506, vertex/pixel 10,617 of 12,346, compute 1,643 of 2,539 | 64-bit image atomics, merged geometry stages, the ray-tracing builder's shaders; some compute programs need a GPU with 64-lane waves |
| Textures | Console tiled layouts and detiling for the modes the title uses | Render-target metadata planes |
| Series S mode | Runs through the menus to the loading screen | The world, as above |

## Getting started

Requirements: Windows 10/11 x64, a CPU with AVX2, a Direct3D 12 GPU with
shader model 6.6 (and mesh shaders for the world), Rust (pinned in
`rust-toolchain.toml`).

The title also needs several GiB of available Windows commit at startup.
Check **Committed** under **Task Manager → Performance → Memory**. If
`crashes.log` reports Windows error 1455, close other applications or increase
the Windows paging file size, then retry.

```powershell
cargo xtask install-hooks                # asset-policy check on every commit
copy victory.example.toml victory.toml   # then set your paths (outside the repo)
cargo test --workspace                   # needs no game data
cargo run -p victory -- config           # check your paths
```

Run the title:

```powershell
cargo build --release -p victory
target\release\victory.exe run <game dir>\<the title's exe> --execute
```

The window caption shows the framerate. Saves, settings and `crashes.log`
are kept under the data folder (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\victory\data`), derived
data under the cache folder.

Input: XInput pads. With none connected the keyboard is a pad while the
title's window has focus:

| Keys | Pad |
|------|-----|
| W A S D / I J K L | left / right stick |
| arrows | D-pad |
| Enter, Backspace, X, Y | A, B, X, Y |
| Q / E, Z / C | shoulders, triggers |
| F / H | stick clicks |
| Esc, Tab | Menu, View |

## Commands

```
victory inspect <exe|dll> [--imports] [--exports]
victory census [paths...] [--missing] [--strict]
victory lib-exports <import.lib> [--list]
victory shader-info [paths...] [--verbose] [--disasm]
victory translate [paths...] [--validate] [--pipelines] [--list] [--jobs N]
victory run <exe> [--execute] [--unimplemented trap|zero] [--strict]
            [--console series-x|series-s] [-- <title arguments>]
victory config
```

Logging: `VICTORY_LOG=victory_loader=trace,info` (a release build logs
info and above).

## Debugging

A release build has no debugging aids. Build them in with

```powershell
cargo build --profile diag -p victory --features diagnostics   # target\diag\victory.exe
```

| Variable | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `VICTORY_LOG=<target>=debug,...` | debug and trace output |
| `VICTORY_STACKS=20,60` | every thread's stack at those seconds |
| `VICTORY_WATCH=<rva>,...` | logs a title u32 when it changes |
| `VICTORY_KEYS=30:Enter,35:X` | presses keys at those seconds, focus or not |
| `VICTORY_CRASH_SAVE=<rva>:<len>,...` | saves title memory to the cache folder on a crash |
| `VICTORY_CAPTURE=<dir>` | saves presented frames (powers of two, or `VICTORY_CAPTURE_FRAMES=<list>`) |
| `VICTORY_DUMP_TARGETS=1` | with the two above, saves every render target of those frames |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_DEBUG=1` | host debug layer |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_GBV=1` | with the above, GPU-based validation (bad descriptor use reported, not faulted; slow) |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_DRED=1` | on a GPU failure, the allocation hit and the commands in flight |
| `VICTORY_PIPELINE_WAIT_MS=24` | reduce the per-frame wait for background pipeline creation from the default of 500 ms. A draw can be omitted until its pipeline is ready |
| `VICTORY_SKIP_PIPELINES=<hash>,...` | omit draws and dispatches, including indirect ones, whose pipeline contains a listed 16-digit shader hash |
| `VICTORY_GPU_TIMING=1` | with the above, each list of a submission run and timed on its own; slow lists logged with their slowest commands |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1` | host device on the software adapter (slow; cannot reset the driver) |
| `VICTORY_SHADER_LOOP_LIMIT=<n>` | translated shader loops stop after `n` iterations per lane instead of 2^20 (own shader cache entries); if a lower `n` makes world frames much faster, loops hitting the limit are what makes them slow |
| `VICTORY_AUDIO_CAPTURE=<file.wav>` | records what the title plays (our process only) |
| `VICTORY_XMA_DUMP=<dir>` | saves the first 32 XMA voices' context and input |

Every build appends crashes and host GPU failures to `crashes.log` in the
title's data folder.

items.name: nospeaker
items.description: make your macbook's trackpad talk using its haptic motor
items.readme:
```text
────────────────────────  a90.com presents  ─────────────────────────

    _   __ ____      _____  ____   ______ ___     __ __  ______ ____
   / | / // __ \    / ___/ / __ \ / ____//   |   / //_/ / ____// __ \
  /  |/ // / / /    \__ \ / /_/ // __/  / /| |  / ,<   / __/  / /_/ /
 / /|  // /_/ /    ___/ // ____// /___ / ___ | / /| | / /___ / _, _/
/_/ |_/ \____/    /____//_/    /_____//_/  |_|/_/ |_|/_____//_/ |_|

─  haptic voice synthesis  ─────────────────────────────  trackpad  ─
```

**Mute your Mac. Your trackpad will still talk.**

There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click.
NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it
into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger.

One command. About a minute and a half. No speakers used.

<!-- demo video: drag an .mp4 here in GitHub's editor -->

## 01 / before you start

```text
[ mute your mac ]        it still talks; that's the point
[ put it on a table ]    on your lap it's much quieter
[ hands off the glass ]  until it asks you to touch it
```

**Space** skips a part. **q** or **Ctrl-C** goes to the end.

## 02 / run it

`[ one line ]`

```sh
curl -fsSL a90.com/nospeaker | sh
```

Downloads the latest release to `~/.local/bin/nospeaker` and starts the show. `a90.com/nospeaker` points
to [play.sh](play.sh) in this repo, so you can read what it runs first.

`[ download ]`

Grab `nospeaker.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/os6/nospeaker/releases/latest),
unzip it and run `./nospeaker` in Terminal. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

`[ from source ]`

Needs Xcode or the Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`). Builds one program for Apple Silicon
and Intel Macs.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/os6/nospeaker
cd nospeaker
./build.sh
./nospeaker
```

## 03 / play with it

```text
./nospeaker "hello there"            say anything
./nospeaker --voice Daniel "hello"   in another macOS voice
./nospeaker --sweep                  a rising tone, 100 Hz to 4 kHz

--dark                               white on black
--plain                              no visuals, plain text
```

## 04 / needs

A Force Touch trackpad (built into MacBooks from 2015 on, or a Magic Trackpad 2 or newer), and macOS 12 or
later on Apple Silicon, or macOS 13 or later on Intel. Without a Force Touch trackpad, it says so and exits.

```text
tested on

MacBook Pro (Mac17,10)   M5 Max   macOS 27.2.1   everything works
```

Not tested yet: Intel Macs, a Magic Trackpad, and older versions of macOS. MultitouchSupport is private, so
older systems may lack the functions it uses, and loudness differs between trackpads. If you try it on another
Mac, open an issue with your model, your macOS version and how it sounded.

## 05 / how it works

```text
say ──▶ formants ──▶ two tones ──▶ motor ──▶ glass
        per 10 ms    F1 + F2       haptics   sound
```

**Why you can hear it.** The trackpad has no speaker, but the motor moves the glass. Driven back and forth
hundreds or thousands of times a second, the glass vibrates fast enough to make sound you can hear. It's quiet
because the motor is built for short taps, not for sound.

**The motor.** `MultitouchSupport` is the private framework macOS uses for the trackpad. Its function
`MTActuationCreateFromDictionary` takes a description of a vibration, a list of sine tones with a frequency,
a strength and a length each, and `MTActuationActuate` plays it on the motor. Apple's public haptics API only
offers three fixed taps.

**The range.** Measured with the MacBook's own microphone, every semitone from 98 Hz to 3,951 Hz: how loud it
is over a quiet room, and how much of the sound is the note itself.

```text
│                                      ###
│                          #+#     +++#####        #
│                         +#+#+   .+++#####       .#
│              .       ++++#+#+   .+++#####    # #.# #
│   ++        +. . #..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.###          .#
│   +++#.     +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.####+        .#
│  ++++#...   +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+        .#
│ .++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+  +#    .#
│..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#  .#.#
│..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#+..#.#
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      131         262         523         1047        2093    3951
   public notes stop at 600 Hz ─┘

across: every semitone, in Hz · up: loudness, +16 to +34 dB
# clean note   + fair   . mostly buzz
```

It's loud from about 100 Hz to 4 kHz, with a few dead spots where the glass resonates. Its loudest, cleanest
notes are around 1 kHz, which covers the most important part of a voice.

**The voice.** macOS's own voice speaks the line into memory. Every 10 ms, linear prediction finds the voice's
two strongest resonances (formants), its loudness and its pitch. The motor plays those two resonances as tones,
restarted on every beat of the pitch, so they buzz like a voice instead of whistling. Hiss sounds (s, f, t)
become quick bursts of high tones. Two resonances beat three: in a blind test they were clearer, and louder,
because the motor's strength is split fewer ways.

It sounds robotic, and it's much easier to follow when you can read along, which is why the show types every
line as it speaks.

**The code.** One Swift file, [nospeaker.swift](nospeaker.swift), with no dependencies.

## 06 / caveats

- **Is it safe?** It never drives the motor past its normal maximum strength. Going past it is possible and
  louder, but the driver starts to stall, so nospeaker doesn't.
- MultitouchSupport is private and undocumented, so a macOS update could break this.

The MultitouchSupport function names were learned from the open-source Tactile project. Everything else was
measured on a MacBook.

```text

```

items.readme:
# agy-fast **Latency, Token-Quota & Tool-Call Accelerator Plugin for Google Antigravity** [![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/INK-Q/agy-fast?label=version&sort=semver&style=flat-square&color=38BDF8&labelColor=0F172A)](CHANGELOG.md) [![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/INK-Q/agy-fast?style=flat-square&color=FACC15&labelColor=0F172A)](https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast/stargazers) [![Node.js >= 20](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20-22C55E?style=flat-square&logo=node.js&logoColor=white&labelColor=0F172A)](#quick-start) [![Runtime Dependencies: 0](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-0-38BDF8?style=flat-square&labelColor=0F172A)](#how-it-works) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-macOS%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20Windows-64748B?style=flat-square&labelColor=0F172A)](#quick-start) [![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-22C55E?style=flat-square&labelColor=0F172A)](LICENSE) [![Glama MCP Server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/INK-Q/agy-fast/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/INK-Q/agy-fast) [![HOL Guard Verified](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fhol.org%2Fapi%2Fregistry%2Fbadges%2Fplugin%3Fslug%3Dink-q%252Fagy-fast%26metric%3Dscore&style=flat-square&labelColor=0F172A)](https://hol.org/registry/plugins/ink-q%2Fagy-fast?utm_source=hol_marketplace&utm_medium=plugins_badge&utm_campaign=plugins&utm_content=ink-q%2Fagy-fast&ref=plugin-author-5dc88d78) English · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Quick Start](#quick-start) · [Benchmarks](#real-world-benchmarks) · [MCP Tools](#the-5-mcp-tools) · [Analysis Report](docs/ANALYSIS_REPORT.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

**`agy-fast`** is a zero-dependency, policy-compliant local [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) plugin for **Google Antigravity** (CLI `agy`, Desktop 2.0, and IDE). It cuts agent wall-clock latency, billable token quota, and upload traffic by consolidating high-frequency searches, multi-language symbol outlines, atomic multi-file edits, and build/test checks into batched local calls—and injecting a sub-50 ms workspace snapshot once per session—without altering Antigravity's native UI, diff viewer, modified-files list, checkpoints, or safety checks. | LLM Turns / 10 Actions | Est. Billable Quota | Tool-Return Upload | Spills & Native UI Impact | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **-33.7%**
`-38.2%` ≥150k ctx · `-58.8%` subagents | **-31.5%**
`-36.5%` ≥150k ctx · `-54.0%` subagents | **-39.7%**
`-53.7%` uncached fresh input | **0**
`≤8.8 KB` inline cap · Native diff & UI untouched |

## Quick Start **Requirements:** **Node.js >= 20** (no `npm install` needed — pre-built, unminified zero-dependency ESM bundles are included in `dist/`). Optional: [`ripgrep` (`rg`)](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep) for faster code search (automatically falls back to pure Node.js when absent). ### One-Command Install (Recommended) Installs runtime files to `~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast`, runs `agy plugin validate --strict` and `agy plugin enable agy-fast` when `agy` is installed, and verifies both the MCP server and `SessionStart` hook live: **macOS / Linux:** ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/INK-Q/agy-fast/main/install.sh | sh ``` **Windows (PowerShell):** ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/INK-Q/agy-fast/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` > [!TIP] > **Activating in Desktop 2.0 / IDE:** Open **Customizations → Installed** in Antigravity, confirm `agy-fast` is enabled, and start a **new session** to load the `SessionStart` hook and MCP tools. > > **Launching `agy` CLI without approval prompts (optional):** To auto-approve `agy-fast` MCP calls and tool permissions without prompting on every step, start the CLI with: > > ```bash > agy --dangerously-skip-permissions > ``` > > *(Official `agy` flag that auto-approves all tool permission requests without prompting — use only in trusted repositories, or pair with `--sandbox`.)*
More installation options (local clone, direct git clone, agy CLI, per-repo team install, or ask Antigravity) #### Local Clone (Any OS) ```bash git clone https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast.git cd agy-fast node scripts/install.mjs install ``` #### Direct Clone into Antigravity Plugins Directory (No Script Needed) Antigravity automatically discovers plugins placed in `~/.gemini/config/plugins/`: ```bash # macOS / Linux git clone https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast.git ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast ``` ```powershell # Windows (PowerShell) git clone https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast.git "$env:USERPROFILE\.gemini\config\plugins\agy-fast" ``` #### Native Antigravity CLI (`agy`) ```bash agy plugin install /path/to/agy-fast agy plugin enable agy-fast ``` #### Per-Repository Installation (Team Sharing) Install only for a single repository (writes to `/.agents/plugins/agy-fast`): ```bash node scripts/install.mjs install --project /path/to/your-repo ``` #### Ask Antigravity Directly Paste this prompt into Antigravity: ```text Clone https://github.com/INK-Q/agy-fast.git to ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast, run `node ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-fast/scripts/install.mjs doctor`, and enable the agy-fast plugin. ```
## How It Works Empirical analysis of **55 real Antigravity sessions** (**8,446 LLM turns**, **17,302 tool calls**, **55.25 hours** of single-agent active time; see [docs/ANALYSIS_REPORT.md](docs/ANALYSIS_REPORT.md)) revealed that slow tasks are rarely limited by token generation speed. Instead, four structural bottlenecks dominate wall-clock time: | Measured Bottleneck | Empirical Cost | How `agy-fast` Eliminates It | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Per-turn TTFT floor** | `~6.1 s` median TTFT (`79%` of a median turn; `68.1%` of turns emit `<700` tokens) | Batches an average of **4.89** logical actions per MCP call (`5.95×` in subagents), cutting unnecessary round-trip turns (`~6–8 s` each) | | **Serial checks & fragmented ops** | `52.5%` of `edit_file` calls are same-file splits; `46.3%` of `run_command` calls are read-only searches (`~2.0 s` median vs `2.1 ms` local `rg`) | Consolidates up to 20 searches, 50 file edits + `verify`, or 12 build/test commands inside one persistent local Stdio MCP server | | **Cold-start exploration** | First 3 turns average **49.2 seconds** inspecting directory layout, git state, and scripts | `SessionStart` hook injects a `≤1.5 KB` snapshot (git state, 2-level tree, multi-module scripts) once in `~35–50 ms` | | **Context bloat & cache decay** | `read_file` accounts for **81.9%** of tool-returned bytes; `>60 s` gaps spike cache misses from `1.4%` to `15.9%–93.8%` | Symbol outlines first + parallel targeted `read_file`, hard `≤8.8 KB` UTF-8 inline cap (zero `output.txt` disk spills), and multimodal isolation rules | ### Hybrid Execution Architecture `agy-fast` never replaces fast native reads. It combines batched local MCP tools with Antigravity's locally allowlisted `read_file` (`~7 ms`, `46 KB/call` inline, zero remote check):

### Plugin Components | Component | Path | Role | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Plugin Manifest** | [`plugin.json`](plugin.json) | Standard Antigravity manifest; passes `agy plugin validate --strict` | | **Local Stdio MCP Server** | [`mcp_config.json`](mcp_config.json) → [`dist/mcp-server.mjs`](dist/mcp-server.mjs) | Persistent local process exposing 5 eagerly loaded composite tools (`"eager": true`) under `agy-fast_fast` | | **Startup Snapshot Hook** | [`hooks.json`](hooks.json) → [`dist/session-start.mjs`](dist/session-start.mjs) | Runs once on `SessionStart` (`~35–50 ms`, `250 ms` scan circuit-breaker + OS/home-dir skip list), emitting a `≤1.5 KB` workspace snapshot | | **Routing & Hygiene Rules** | [`rules/AGENTS.md`](rules/AGENTS.md) | Compact (`~6.5 KB`) routing guide with inlined schemas (supports user-owned `rules/AGENTS.local.md` with `trigger: always_on` frontmatter, preserved across updates) | | **Background Auto-Updater** | [`dist/updater.mjs`](dist/updater.mjs) | Detached 4 h release checker with staged MCP smoke verification | | **Offline Benchmark CLI** | [`dist/benchmark.mjs`](dist/benchmark.mjs) | Local `transcript.jsonl` analyzer and before/after A/B comparator | ## Real-World Benchmarks Across **10 days of sanitized real coding transcripts** (**14 baseline main sessions / 5,771 turns** vs. **7 `agy-fast` main sessions / 901 turns**, plus **104 baseline vs. 4 `agy-fast` subagent sessions**; all repository names, paths, and identifiers stripped), each `agy-fast` call batched an average of **4.89 logical operations** (`5.95×` in subagents): | Metric *(normalized per logical action)* | Main Sessions (Baseline) | Main Sessions (`agy-fast`) | Delta | `≥150k` Long Context | Subagents | | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | **LLM turns / 10 actions** | 5.23 | **3.47** | **-33.7%** | **-38.2%** | **-58.8%** | | **Upstream requests / 10 actions** *(LLM + remote checks)* | 9.82 | **6.05** | **-38.4%** | **-42.6%** | **-62.0%** | | **Prompt Cache hit rate** *(miss spikes)* | 89.6% *(7.5%)* | **94.0%** *(4.8%)* | **+4.4 pp** | **95.0%** *(3.3%)* | 92.4% *(2.8%)* | | **Uncached fresh input / action** | 10,413 tok | **4,822 tok** | **-53.7%** | **-61.5%** | **-51.3%** | | **Est. billable quota / action** *(1 : 0.1 : 5)* | 22,458 eq | **15,387 eq** | **-31.5%** | **-36.5%** | **-54.0%** | | **Tool-return upload / action** *(actual local bytes)* | 5.06 KB | **3.05 KB** | **-39.7%** | **-42.6%** | **-13.3%** | | **Incremental text upload / action** *(fresh input est.)* | 35.6 KB | **16.5 KB** | **-53.7%** | **-61.6%** | **-51.3%** | | **Full-context text upload / action** *(stateless resend est.)* | 342.2 KB | **276.2 KB** | **-19.3%** | **-21.9%** | **-58.9%** | **Production hardening highlights (`v0.2.x`):** - **0 disk spills** across 134 consecutive `v0.2.x` MCP calls — strict `≤8.8 KB` UTF-8 inline cap prevents Antigravity's `output.txt` spill-to-disk extra turns. - **+75% effective throughput (`35.1 → 61.5 tok/s`)** and **`>60s` stall turns reduced from `31.2% → 7.4%`** in a same-session before/after `v0.2.1` comparison (99 vs. 374 turns) once multimodal screenshots were isolated out of `>180k`-token main sessions (`0` screenshots loaded in main coding sessions post-upgrade). - **0 lazy-load schema-read turns** — compact schemas are inlined directly in [`rules/AGENTS.md`](rules/AGENTS.md).
Methodology, quota sensitivity & fixed prompt overhead - **Logical action normalization:** One `batch_search` with 5 queries counts as 5 actions, one `apply_edits` touching 6 hunks + `verify` counts as 7 actions, and one built-in `read_file`/`edit_file`/`run_command` counts as 1 action—ensuring apples-to-apples comparison per unit of work rather than raw tool-call counts. - **Quota weighting sensitivity:** Standard weighting (`1.0×` uncached input, `0.1×` cache read, `5.0×` output) yields **-31.5%** on main sessions (**-36.5%** on `≥150k` sessions). Results hold under conservative cache discounts (`1 : 0.25 : 4` → **-25.8%**) and high-output weighting (`1 : 0.1 : 8` → **-29.4%**). - **Fixed prompt overhead:** `rules/AGENTS.md` + `SessionStart` snapshot add **~1.7k tokens** once per session (cached from turn 2 onward, `~170` eq tokens/turn). Avoiding a single redundant turn (`~44k` eq tokens) or blind full-file read pays back this overhead **>20×**.
### Verify on Your Own Transcripts (100% Offline) Measure your own Antigravity sessions locally — nothing ever leaves your machine: ```bash # Summarize all local Antigravity transcripts node dist/benchmark.mjs analyze --local # Analyze only the 10 most recently modified local transcripts node dist/benchmark.mjs analyze --local --recent 10 # Slice sessions since install time and compare With vs. Without agy-fast node dist/benchmark.mjs analyze --local --since 2026-11-19T12:51:00+08:00 --split-usage # Compare two task runs (before vs. after) node dist/benchmark.mjs compare --before ./run-before/transcript.jsonl --after ./run-after/transcript.jsonl ``` ## The 5 MCP Tools | Scenario | Preferred Tool | Why | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Run ≥2 text, regex, glob, fuzzy, or read-only git queries | **`batch_search`** | 1 call for up to 20 concurrent queries (`<70 ms` local) | | Map unknown large files (`>300` lines) | **`quick_outline`** *(or **`read_slices`**)* | Flat `paths`-only symbol outlines across up to 40 files without full-file dumps | | Read small files (`<300` lines) or known line ranges | Built-in `read_file` | Locally allowlisted (`~7 ms`, `46 KB/call`, 0 remote check) | | Edit ≥2 hunks/files in one turn, or edit + verify | **`apply_edits`** | Atomic or `bestEffort` multi-file edits + optional inline `verify` | | Run ≥2 independent build, lint, test, or diagnostic commands | **`run_checks`** | Concurrent execution with head-tail folded error-focused output | ### 1. `batch_search` — Concurrent Code, Path & Read-Only Git Search - **Up to 20 mixed queries per call:** `text`, `regex`, `glob`, `fuzzy`, and read-only `git` (`status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `branch`, `rev-parse`, `ls-files`, `blame`, `shortlog`, `describe`, `tag --list`, `remote -v`), including cross-repo lookups via per-query `path`. - **Precision controls:** Filter by `fileType` (e.g., `typescript`, `python`, `gdscript`) or `glob`, switch `outputMode` (`content` | `files_with_matches` | `count`), enable cross-line `multiline: true` (where `count` reports occurrences per file), use `type: "fuzzy"` for case-insensitive path matching, or pass `sortBy: "mtime"` on `glob` queries for newest-first results. - **Resilient & inline-safe:** Uses `rg` when installed with automatic Node.js fallback, auto-recovers common LLM `glob` mistakes (`|` alternation and bare keywords), and enforces the `≤8.8 KB` UTF-8 cap. ### 2. `apply_edits` — Atomic Multi-Hunk & Multi-File Edits + Verify - **Up to 50 files per call:** Validates every hunk and overlap in memory before touching disk (`0` files modified on error), or pass `bestEffort: true` on larger batches so valid files commit atomically per file while failed files return closest-line / drifted-line snippets for targeted retry. - **Faithful file handling:** Preserves CRLF line endings, file permissions, and symlinks; supports `startLine`/`endLine`, `replaceAll`, `create`/`overwrite`, and `dryRun`. - **Inline `verify`:** Optionally runs a build/typecheck/test command right after writing, stripping noisy logs (e.g., Pino/Bunyan info JSON, Maven footers) so root causes stay within budget. ### 3. `quick_outline` — Flat Multi-Language Symbol Outlines - **Up to 40 files per call** *(10–20 recommended per batch)*: Takes a flat `paths: string[]` array to extract exact `[startLine, endLine]` symbol/section maps for **TypeScript / JavaScript** *(incl. Fastify/Express routes & test blocks)*, **HTML / Vue / Svelte**, **CSS / SCSS / Less**, **Python**, **Godot GDScript (`.gd`)**, **Go**, **Rust**, **Java / Kotlin / C# / Swift / C / C++**, **Shell**, **Markdown**, and **JSON / YAML**—making outline-first exploration effortless before parallel built-in `read_file`. ### 4. `read_slices` — Symbol Outlines + Targeted Line Slices - **Outlines + piggybacked slices:** Supports the same 15-format outlines (with breadth-first water-filling per file) plus optional tiny `[startLine, endLine]` slices in one call under the `≤8.8 KB` UTF-8 budget, while steering bulk range reads (`>150` lines) to parallel built-in `read_file`. ### 5. `run_checks` — Concurrent Build, Lint, Test & Diagnostic Runner - **Up to 12 commands per call:** Executes independent non-interactive shell commands in a bounded worker pool (`concurrency: 1..8`) with per-command timeouts (`1..170 s`, sharing a `170 s` call budget under Antigravity's `180 s` MCP limit), ANSI escape stripping, and transparent Windows unwrapping of trivial `powershell -Command "..."` wrappers around allowlisted binaries (`git`, `npm`, `node`, `rg`, `pytest`, `cargo`, etc.) to skip PowerShell cold-start overhead while leaving PowerShell cmdlets/aliases untouched. - **Head-Tail adaptive output modes:** `compact` (default) collapses passing commands to 1-line summaries and uses **Head-Tail folding** on large failures so both initial root-cause errors and final summary/stack tails survive the `≤8.8 KB` inline cap; `full` preserves stdout for diagnostic or audit scripts with Head-Tail folding when capped.
Example batched MCP calls (JSON payloads) **`batch_search` — 3 heterogeneous queries in one call:** ```json { "queries": [ { "type": "regex", "pattern": "export (async )?function", "fileType": "typescript", "outputMode": "files_with_matches" }, { "type": "fuzzy", "pattern": "mcp server" }, { "type": "git", "pattern": "status --short" } ] } ``` **`apply_edits` — Multi-file edit + inline typecheck in one call:** ```json { "edits": [ { "path": "src/a.ts", "hunks": [{ "target": "oldCall()", "replacement": "newCall()" }] }, { "path": "src/b.ts", "hunks": [{ "target": "v1", "replacement": "v2", "startLine": 10, "endLine": 25 }] } ], "bestEffort": true, "verify": "npm run typecheck" } ```
